statement.p: Two particles are traveling through space. At time t the first particle is at the point (2 + t, -4 + 2 t, 5 - 2 t) and the second particle is at (-8 + 3 t, -9 + 3 t, 10 - 3 t)
Describe the two paths in words. Then determine if the two particles collide, cross, or neither cross nor collide to fill in the following.

We see that
?
the paths cross, and the particles collide there
the paths of the particles cross, but with no collision
neither of these is true .
If they collide or their paths cross, indicate where (if neither is true, enter none).
A collision or crossing occurs at (x,y,z) = .

p.m: \text{the paths cross, and the particles collide there}

static.solution:
(2,-4,5) in the direction of the vector \vec i + 2 \vec j - 2 \vec k and the second passes through (-8,-9,10) in the direction of the vector 3 \vec i + 3 \vec j - 3 \vec k. The two paths are not parallel.
Is there a time t when the two particles are at the same place at the same time? If so, then the particles collide, and their coordinates will be the same. Equating coordinates, we get 2 + t = -8 + 3 t, \quad -4 + 2 t = -9 + 3 t,\quad 5 - 2 t = 10 - 3 t.
Since all three equations are solved by t=5, the two particles do in fact arrive at the same place at the same time, and so they do collide.
Then, the two paths cross if there are times t_1 and t_2 such that the position of the first particle at time t_1 is the same as the position of the second particle at time t_2. In this case this is obvious: when t_1 = t_2 = 5, the paths cross.
